# Review and Optional AI Assistance {#sec-review}

## Inspect the image

**Purpose.** Inspect the retinal image and any optional model evidence before the grade decision. No clinical decision is recorded on this page.

![Review page: image on the left, optional model evidence and the single forward action on the right.](screenshots/03-review-overview.png){#fig-review width=90%}

**Steps.**

1. Review opens after **Confirm Image**. You can also open it with **Review** in a confirmed Worklist row.
2. Check the **Patient/Eye** line above the image.
3. Use the viewer controls to zoom, fit, pan, inspect coordinates, or open the full-screen view.
4. Choose a viewer mode below the image: **Original**, **AI evidence**, or, when PRISM recorded one, **PRISM analysis field**. **More views** adds **Explainability** and, for an ultra-widefield image, **Analysis area** and **Mask preview**.
5. In **Analysis**, read the **AI status** badge: **AI READY** or **AI UNAVAILABLE**. It refreshes on its own while the page is open. Choose **Analyze** (or **Analyze again**) when offered. When PRISM needs its own prepared input, the button reads **Analyze grading only** and runs DR grading alone.
6. Choose **Continue to clinician review**. This is the only forward action on Review; nothing is recorded on this page.

**Expected result.** The retinal image stays the main surface. The right column shows **Analysis**, **DR assessment**, and **Lesion suggestions**. Technical provenance (image ID, dimensions, source, transforms, mask, and model versions) is kept under **Processing details**; choose **Show details** to open it. **Previous exam comparison** opens with **Show comparison**. Annotation work is not started from Review; it follows the grade decision (@sec-annotations).

## Prepare PRISM input

PRISM lesion suggestions use a one-time prepared input, separate from grading. Choose **Preview PRISM input** below the image.

PRISM preparation requires confirmed image quality. If quality was not recorded at Confirm Image, the panel says *Confirm image quality before using PRISM.* and offers **Image quality acceptable** below the reviewer name. For an image recorded as not usable, it says so and offers **Change to quality acceptable**; use it only if the image quality really is acceptable.

**Prepare / refresh API input** distinguishes planned API submission from a conditional FOV candidate; native ROI is **NOT_RUN**, so the final internal crop is not previewed. Only a server-verified receipt from a compatible provider can offer **Submit prepared input to PRISM**, after input acknowledgement. Current production adapters are not qualified for this path; if preparation is unavailable, continue with manual review. Input acknowledgement does not confirm a medical finding.

The workstation routes model assistance from the clinician-confirmed image type
and the live capability metadata. A ready global capability must advertise
`CFP` for CFP grading or `UWF` for UWF grading. `Other / Unknown` is
manual-only, and PRISM is lesion assistance rather than a DR grading model.
The Settings page shows the discovered task, modality, readiness, and release
state. AI availability never changes the clinician's final decision path.

For an **Ultra-widefield** image, Review remains available whether or not a
ready UWF capability is connected. The UI enables model assistance only when
the live metadata advertises a compatible ready capability. PRISM UWF lesion
assistance is experimental, was trained for CFP, and is **not validated for
UWF**. If PRISM reports that a trusted analysis field was used, **PRISM
analysis field** shows the same-size field evidence associated with that
inference. When processing falls back to the Original image, no PRISM boundary
is drawn; **Processing details** reports that fallback processing was used.
These are previous-run processing records, not a preview of the next request.
If native ROI fails, the baseline discards its FOV candidate and uses full Original.
FOV or native ROI preparation failure alone does not mean inference failed.
The mask is an engineering aid, not a diagnosis or a validated lesion
segmentation; human review remains authoritative.

## Read the model suggestions

- **DR assessment** shows the **System-predicted DR grade** and the **Top model score**. This is a model score, not a calibrated probability.
- **Lesion suggestions** counts PRISM-DR suggestions by class. An untouched overlay is labelled with class and score, for example `EX 0.82`.
- Each result names its model in plain words, for example *AI: RETFound (CFP grading)*, *AI: USPEC (UWF grading)*, or *AI: PRISM (lesion suggestions)*. Model IDs and versions are under **Processing details**.
- The lesion summary is not a task list. You do not need to inspect every AI ROI.

## Show or filter the overlays

Choose **AI evidence** to show the PRISM overlays and **Original** to hide them. In AI evidence mode, the lesion filter displays **All lesion classes** or one class: **MA: Microaneurysm**, **HE: Hemorrhage**, **EX: Hard exudate**, or **SE: Soft exudate**. The line below reads *Active overlays N of M raw AI suggestions*.

![Overlay controls below the viewer.](screenshots/04-ai-controls.png){#fig-ai-controls width=80%}
